---
title: "Recycling pads the shorter vector without warning"
ref: IDX-04
categories: [Indexing]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'c(2, 1, 1, 2) == c(1, 2)'
reponse: 'FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE'
attendu: "`TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE`, each value being 1 or 2"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
values <- c(2, 1, 1, 2)
values == c(1, 2)

1:6 + 1:2
1:5 + 1:2
```
:::

## Why

When two vectors of different lengths meet, R repeats the shorter one until it reaches the length of the longer. `values == c(1, 2)` therefore compares element by element with `1, 2, 1, 2`, which has nothing to do with "belongs to".

R only warns when the longer length is not a multiple of the shorter, as for `1:5 + 1:2`. In every other case, recycling goes unnoticed.

## The fix

To test membership, use `%in%`. For a calculation, check that lengths are equal before combining: `stopifnot()` then stops the script instead of recycling.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
values %in% c(1, 2)

a <- 1:6
b <- 1:2
stopifnot(length(a) == length(b))
```
:::
